features.note: The OFF/FULL pair (exhaust-off vs exhaust-full) genuinely works: exhaust-off shows a flush louver panel with near-closed horizontal blades and two dark fan ports; exhaust-full shows the same panel with the blades visibly TILTED open, revealing depth and gaps, plus the two circular fan openings. That state change is convincing. But the enclosure itself reads weakly as a WALLED room: in compressor-room and compressor-room-open the packages sit on the slab under the trunk pipe with the bay's own grey walls behind them, and I cannot see the enclosure walls toggle ON vs OFF between those two frames - they look nearly identical. The louvered wall in exhaust-* is a single detached-looking panel on a plain box, not clearly a room boundary heat crosses. Present but requires inferring the enclosure from separate frames; that lowers it below threshold.

Identity is strong: in luminaire-grid the fixtures are clearly cylindrical UFO highbays - dark finned/canopy body with a bright white lit lens on the underside - not emissive boxes and not scattered. In luminaire-plan I can COUNT roughly 6 rows down the bay (approx y-bands at the truss lines) with about 3 columns across; I can positively count ~13-15 discrete fixture discs and infer the remainder to reach 18. The array reads REGULAR and column-aligned. Count is partly inferred rather than fully countable, but pattern + fixture identity carry it just over threshold.

ahu-roof shows the AHU (dark box with blue-tinted access panel) with a round vertical riser dropping to the horizontal trunk duct below (metallic cylinder with green flow arrows), plus a separate condenser box with two roof fans joined by orange refrigerant lines - a continuous, sensibly routed path. duct-run and hero confirm the trunk runs the length of the bay with hex fittings/branch points (green markers) along it. No floating duct segments spotted; the riser-to-trunk connection is legible. Diffuser drops to the occupied space are not distinctly visible, which is the main weakness, but the air path is continuous.

In compressor-skid all four elements ARE in frame without cropping: two dark packages (lead + lag) each with a circular cooling-fan grille, one tall dark-blue vertical receiver with a domed top, and a small box to the right serving as the dryer, with thin silver piping linking package tops to the receiver. However identity quality is poor: the compressor packages read as plain black cubes with a single grille rather than rotary-screw canopies; the dryer is an anonymous small box with no distinguishing features; and the connecting piping is thin, sparse, toy-like rod rather than real process piping. It reads as generic boxes, not a recognizable rotary-screw skid - below threshold on identity even though the inventory is complete.

hero shows an elongated clad-wall volume with a roof-level grid of dark beams and vertical posts - proportions read like a long low industrial bay (consistent with 40x20x8). Interior frames (luminaire-grid) are more convincing: visible ceiling deck, crossing structural beams, columns and clad walls give a real building interior. But in hero the roof is a flat lattice of thin bars rather than legible trusses, and with no roof cladding the shell reads partly as an open-topped box. Column grid is present but faint. Reads as a building, but the hollow-box impression from hero keeps it just under threshold.

important_features.note: compressor-room-open and hero show a silver header rising from the vertical receiver up to the black high-level trunk that runs the length of the bay with directional flow cones - sensibly routed at high level. Reads acceptably.

A small tan/gold human figure appears on the slab in duct-run, ahu-roof and luminaire-plan, but it is crude (a peg body with a ball head) and very small in frame, so it only weakly makes the 8 m height legible. Present but low-fidelity.

defects.detail: compressor-room (walls ON) and compressor-room-open (walls OFF) look nearly identical; the enclosure never reads as a walled room around the packages - the louvered panel in exhaust-* looks like a detached box face rather than a room boundary. The damper state change is fine; the room is not.

In compressor-skid the two compressor packages are plain black cubes with a single circular grille; nothing reads as a rotary-screw canopy. The dryer is an anonymous box. Connecting piping is thin rod, not process piping.
In hero the roof is a flat grid of thin bars with no cladding, giving a hollow open-topped-box impression; trusses are not legible as trusses.
The human figure is a peg-and-ball shape, tiny in every frame it appears in; weak scale cue.

corrections.action: Give the enclosure four legible clad walls with the louver+fans set into an exterior wall, and make the walls-ON/OFF toggle visibly add/remove those walls in compressor-room vs compressor-room-open so the boundary is unmistakable.

Model the packages as rotary-screw canopies (louvered/finned side grille, control-panel face, base skid) and give the dryer a distinguishing form (refrigerated-dryer body with cooling coil face). Replace the thin rod piping with sized headers and elbows joining lead/lag -> receiver -> dryer.
Add roof cladding or legible trusses so the shell does not read as an open box, and/or frame hero slightly lower so the column grid and roof plane are clearly a closed building.
Use a higher-fidelity ~1.8 m human silhouette and place it beside the compressor skid or bay wall in at least one hero-scale frame.
